name: Reasoning RAG via System 1 or System 2: A Survey on Reasoning Agentic Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Industry Challenges (Liang et al.)
venue: arXiv preprint arXiv:2506.10408 (v1 submitted 12 Jun 2025). Subjects: cs.AI (primary), cs.IR. arXiv-issued DOI 10.48550/arXiv.2506.10408. Not formally peer-reviewed at a conference/journal as of this record; positioned as an industry-oriented survey.
authors_affiliation: Jintao Liang (Beijing University of Posts and Telecommunications); Gang Su (University of Georgia); Huifeng Lin, You Wu (South China University of Technology); Rui Zhao (SenseTime Research & Qingyuan Research Institute, Shanghai Jiao Tong University); Ziyue Li (corresponding author; Technical University of Munich & University of Cologne). 6 authors across Chinese, German and US institutions.
code_url: N/A (survey, no method code). Companion paper list: https://github.com/ByebyeMonica/Reasoning-Agentic-RAG
maintained_repo_url: https://github.com/ByebyeMonica/Reasoning-Agentic-RAG (companion GitHub paper list curating representative Predefined-Reasoning and Agentic-Reasoning papers plus open-source Agentic RAG projects; ~28 stars, last updated around May 2025, so only lightly maintained vs the frozen PDF).
task_domain: Survey of Reasoning Agentic RAG. Primary surveyed task is knowledge-intensive / open-domain QA and multi-hop reasoning, framed for industry challenges; explicitly motivated by multi-document synthesis, legal/biomedical QA, multi-modal (tables/charts/images) enterprise intelligence, scientific reporting, technical support, deep research, and strategic/multi-step decision-making. Spans QA, retrieval, tool-use and web search rather than embodied/robotics.
problem_setting: A literature review (not a method). It synthesizes the shift from static/basic RAG pipelines to Reasoning Agentic RAG, where decision-making and adaptive tool use are embedded directly into the retrieval process. It defines two top-level paradigms - (1) Predefined Reasoning: fixed, modular, rule-based pipelines (query reformulation, retrieval, re-ranking, generation under static control logic), aligned with cognitive System 1 (fast, structured); and (2) Agentic Reasoning: the LLM acts as an autonomous agent that dynamically decides when/what/how to retrieve and interact with tools during inference, aligned with System 2 (slow, deliberate, model-driven). The surveyed setting is predominantly single-agent (one LLM agent orchestrating retrieval/tools), interactive/iterative at inference time, over external corpora or live search engines; supervision ranges from training-free prompting (off-the-shelf LRMs/function-calling) to RL-trained search agents. DeepResearcher is noted as a multi-agent (reasoning + browsing agents) exception.
what_is_retrieved: Predominantly external documents / passages / chunks from knowledge bases and live search engines. The survey also covers retrieving via tool/API calls (function calling, search APIs, structured database queries) and, for tree-based methods, hierarchical document summaries (RAPTOR). It is a document/tool-retrieval survey, not an experience/case/skill-memory survey; demos/trajectories/skills are not the retrieval target.
retrieval_grounding: Predominantly STATIC external corpus (local document collections, knowledge bases) and live external search engines (web/PubMed). The dominant grounding is a fixed external knowledge source queried at inference; there is no agent-written growing episodic memory as the central object (no experience write-back store). So grounding = static external corpus / live search engine, not growing memory.
completeness_vs_topk_objective: The canonical objective surveyed is top-k retrieval by relevance (BM25/dense top-k), refined by re-ranking, corrective filtering (CRAG), and iterative/agentic multi-turn retrieval that progressively expands coverage across reasoning steps. Training-based agents optimize retrieval-quality metrics (recall@k, NDCG, Hits@N for DeepRetrieval) and final-answer correctness rather than recovering a fixed complete minimal set. Multi-hop/agentic loops pursue sufficiency-of-evidence across turns rather than per-call set completeness; not framed as precision-driven variable-size recommendation.
retrieval_unit: Surveyed as a spectrum: document / passage / text chunk (the dominant unit for both predefined and agentic methods); hierarchical document-summary nodes in tree-based RAPTOR; tool/search-API call as a retrieval action in agentic reasoning (search query encapsulated in special <search> tokens for RL agents); and structured-database query results. The default unit is the retrieved document/chunk; agentic methods add the tool-call/search-query as the operative unit.
index_source: Surveyed across the spectrum but dominantly static offline-built corpora indexed for retrieval (local retrieval systems for Search-R1/R1-Searcher/ReZero) and live external/real-world search engines (restricted PubMed for DeepRetrieval; open web search APIs for DeepResearcher). The store is read-only/external; there is no online experience-induced growing memory. So index source = static external corpus or live web search engine, constructed offline / queried online, not agent-grown.
index_structure_topology: Surveyed: flat retrieval indices (BM25 sparse / dense semantic vector indices, the basic-RAG default); refined indexing with fine-grained chunking and metadata-aware retrieval (Advanced RAG); hierarchical / recursive TREE structures (RAPTOR's recursive summary tree); and modular/LEGO-like configurable pipelines (Modular-RAG) rather than a single index topology. Agentic methods treat the search engine/API as an external black-box index. No knowledge-graph index is a focus.
retriever_type: Surveyed broadly: sparse keyword retrieval (BM25, the Naive-RAG default), dense semantic retrievers (Advanced RAG), and live search engines / search APIs invoked as tools (function calling, web search). Agentic training-based methods add LLM-as-query-generator / LLM-as-policy that reformulates queries (DeepRetrieval) or decides when to call a fixed retriever (Search-R1). No single retriever is endorsed; the survey catalogs sparse, dense, and tool/search-engine retrievers.
retriever_learning_signal: Surveyed across the full range and this is a central axis. Predefined-reasoning / prompt-based methods use off-the-shelf retrievers (none / frozen BM25 or dense). Training-based agentic methods learn retrieval/query behavior via REINFORCEMENT LEARNING (PPO / GRPO): Search-R1 and R1-Searcher use outcome-based answer reward (+ format/retrieval rewards) to learn when/what to search; DeepRetrieval rewards retrieval metrics (recall@k, NDCG, Hits@N) of the executed query; ReZero adds a retry reward for productive persistence; DeepResearcher uses F1-based answer reward in live web environments. So signal spans none/off-the-shelf to RL-trained search/query policies.
query_construction: Surveyed: raw query (basic RAG); query reformulation / rewriting (Modular-RAG module; DeepRetrieval learns to rewrite queries via RL to maximize retrieval metrics); sub-question decomposition (Self-Ask generates and answers follow-up questions); thought-conditioned mid-generation queries (ReAct's Thought->Action->Search; Search-o1 triggers search on self-assessed knowledge gaps); and learned search-token emission (<search>...</search> in Search-R1/ReZero). Spans raw, reformulated, decomposed, and reasoning-state-conditioned query construction.
query_granularity: Surveyed at multiple levels. Predefined route-based methods decide retrieval at the task/turn level (RAGate per dialogue turn; Self-Route per query). Loop/agentic methods construct queries at the reasoning-step level (Self-RAG mid-generation; ReAct per Thought-Action step; Search-R1 emits search queries interleaved with <think> steps across a multi-turn trajectory). So task-level, turn-level, and step/trajectory-level query granularity are all covered.
when_to_retrieve: Surveyed as the organizing distinction. Predefined reasoning: route-based conditional triggering (one-shot decision on whether to retrieve), loop-based iterative refinement, tree-based recursive/hierarchical, and hybrid-modular routing. Agentic reasoning: active/adaptive, agent-initiated retrieval where the LLM autonomously decides WHEN and WHAT to retrieve during its reasoning trajectory (ReAct, Search-o1, Search-R1). Overall spans one-shot/route -> iterative/loop -> active agent-initiated -> learned RL policy.
retrieval_trigger_signal: Surveyed concrete WHEN-to-retrieve signals: model confidence / uncertainty estimation and conversation context (RAGate route-based; Self-Route confidence-based routing between RAG and Long-Context); retrieval-quality evaluator scores categorizing chunks as correct/incorrect/ambiguous (CRAG); reflection / self-critique decisions mid-generation (Self-RAG); learned query-complexity routing (Adaptive-RAG); self-assessed knowledge gaps in a reasoning chain (ReAct Thought, Search-o1); and learned policy emitting special <search> tokens (Search-R1, ReZero, with retry-triggered re-search in ReZero). So signal spans confidence/uncertainty, evaluator scores, reflection, learned complexity classifier, and agent-initiated/learned-policy triggers.
reranking: Yes - re-ranking is surveyed as a core component of Advanced/Modular RAG (a dedicated module for ranking/filtering retrieved results in the Modular-RAG pipeline; dense re-ranking and multi-hop querying in Advanced RAG). CRAG's lightweight retrieval evaluator acts as a corrective relevance assessor. Re-ranking is presented as one of the swappable modules rather than a single prescribed reranker type.
retrieved_context_refinement: Surveyed across operations: corrective filtering and query rewriting / web-search fallback when retrieved chunks are low quality (CRAG); recursive abstractive summarization of retrieved content into a tree (RAPTOR); a Reason-in-Documents module that distills retrieved content into a refined, denoised format to preserve reasoning integrity (Search-o1); retrieved-token masking during RL loss to stabilize training (Search-R1); and module-level filtering/ranking in Modular-RAG. The survey explicitly flags the lost-in-the-middle problem and need for adaptive context management. So refinement spans rerank/filter, distill/reason-in-documents, summarize, and compress.
how_retrieved_used: Predominantly prompt augmentation: retrieved documents are injected into the LLM context for grounded generation (basic/predefined RAG). Agentic reasoning interleaves retrieval as an action within the reasoning trajectory (ReAct Observation feeds subsequent Thought; Search-R1 places retrieved content in <information> tags consumed by further reasoning). Training-based methods additionally use retrieval outcomes as the RL TRAINING SIGNAL (reward) to shape the search policy. So usage spans prompt augmentation, interleaved tool-result consumption, and retrieval-as-reward-signal.
planning_integration: Surveyed across the predefined/agentic split. Predefined: retrieve-then-reason within fixed pipelines, route-then-retrieve (RAGate/Adaptive-RAG router selects path), loop/iterative refine (Self-RAG/CRAG), and tree/MCTS search (RAPTOR recursive tree; MCTS-RAG embeds retrieval inside a Monte Carlo Tree Search loop). Agentic: reasoning and retrieval are tightly interleaved per step (ReAct Thought-Action-Observation; Search-o1; Search-R1 interleaves <think>/<search>/<information>); DeepResearcher plans and dynamically adjusts plans during web research. So integration spans retrieve-then-plan, plan-then-retrieve, per-step interleaved, and inside-tree-search (MCTS-RAG).
reasoning_search_interleaving_granularit: Surveyed at several granularities: per-answer / per-turn (route-based predefined methods retrieve once per query/turn); per-reasoning-step / per-CoT-step (loop-based Self-RAG, ReAct interleaves reasoning steps with retrieval actions, Search-R1 interleaves <think> and <search> across a multi-turn trajectory); and per-tool-call within a rollout (function calling, RL search agents emit search calls inside the reasoning rollout). The agentic paradigm is characterized by tight per-step / per-tool-call interleaving of reasoning and search.
retrieved_item_representation: Predominantly raw retrieved document/passage text injected into context. Higher-abstraction surface forms surveyed: recursive document summaries (RAPTOR tree nodes); a distilled/denoised representation produced by Search-o1's Reason-in-Documents module; and structured tool/API call results. The dominant injected form is raw retrieved text, with summarized/distilled variants for tree-based and reason-in-documents methods.
abstraction_level_of_retrieved_unit: Mostly raw retrieved passages/documents (this is document RAG, not strategy/skill retrieval). Higher-abstraction units surveyed: hierarchical summary nodes (RAPTOR recursive abstractive summaries) and distilled refined evidence (Search-o1 Reason-in-Documents). No distilled strategies, reusable workflows, or procedural skills are retrieved in the agentic-experience sense; abstraction tops out at document summaries.
noise_robustness_mechanism: Surveyed explicitly: a retrieval evaluator that scores chunk quality (correct/incorrect/ambiguous) and triggers corrective query rewriting or web search (CRAG); self-reflection / critique during generation (Self-RAG); a Reason-in-Documents distillation module that filters verbose/noisy/contradictory retrieved content to preserve reasoning integrity, addressing the lost-in-the-middle problem (Search-o1); cross-validation across multiple web sources and self-reflection on contradictory evidence as emergent behaviors (DeepResearcher); and retrieved-token masking to stabilize RL training (Search-R1). So robustness spans relevance evaluation, self-reflection, reason-in-documents refinement, and cross-validation.
memory_type: Mostly none in the classic experiential-memory sense (the survey centers retrieval over external corpora/search engines, not an agent-written memory store). Structural 'memory' analogs surveyed are the hierarchical document-summary tree (RAPTOR) and the multi-turn reasoning context (interleaved <think>/<information> trajectory). No episodic experience memory, skill library, or workflow memory is a central object. So memory_type = none/external-corpus-centric (with a document-summary tree as the closest structured store).
write_back: Mostly false. The surveyed paradigm retrieves from a fixed external corpus or live search engine and does not write experiences/cases/skills back into a persistent memory. RL training updates the agent's policy weights (a form of learning), but there is no experiential memory write-back store. So write_back = false for the surveyed methods (no episodic/case/skill write-back).
online_growth: Predominantly false. The retrievable store is a static external corpus or a live (externally maintained) search engine; the agent does not grow its own retrievable memory at test time. Live web search reflects external content changes but is not agent-authored growth. So online_growth = no (no agent-driven test-time store growth).
write_back_trigger: Never (for an agent-written experience store). The surveyed methods do not log success/failure experiences into a retrievable memory; there is no on-success/on-failure/reflective write trigger. The only analog is offline construction of document summary trees (RAPTOR), built once, not triggered by deployment events. So write_back_trigger = never / N/A.
failure_experience_usage: Not a focus as stored experience. The survey covers handling failed RETRIEVALS within a trajectory rather than storing failed experiences: CRAG corrects when retrieval is judged incorrect/ambiguous; ReZero adds a retry reward incentivizing 'trying one more time' after an unsuccessful initial search (conditioned on eventual task success); DeepResearcher self-reflects and refines search strategies when evidence is contradictory/insufficient. These shape in-trajectory behavior / RL reward, not a success-vs-failure experience memory.
memory_evolution_update: N/A / append-only-offline. No stored experiential entries are mutated over deployment (no episodic memory). The closest analog is RAPTOR's offline recursive summarization that builds the tree once. So memory_evolution_update = N/A (no online entry mutation).
retrieval_as_learned_policy: Surveyed as a major axis and the defining feature of training-based agentic reasoning: retrieval/search IS a learned RL-optimized policy in Search-R1 (outcome reward, PPO/GRPO), R1-Searcher (two-stage outcome-based RL), ReZero (adds retry reward, GRPO), DeepRetrieval (query rewriting rewarded by retrieval metrics, PPO), and DeepResearcher (GRPO with F1 answer reward in live web). In contrast, predefined-reasoning and prompt-based agentic methods use fixed/heuristic top-k or prompt-driven retrieval rather than a learned policy. So the survey explicitly contrasts fixed-retrieval vs learned-retrieval-policy.
cross_agent_or_cross_framework_sharing: Largely N/A / single-agent. Most surveyed methods are single-agent (one LLM orchestrating retrieval/tools). DeepResearcher uses a multi-agent architecture (a reasoning module plus dedicated browsing agents) within one framework, but this is intra-framework task division, not cross-agent or cross-framework experience/memory sharing. No shared collective memory across heterogeneous frameworks is surveyed.
benchmarks: The survey does not run its own experiments and does not consolidate a benchmark table; it references benchmarks via the cited methods. Knowledge-intensive / open-domain QA and multi-hop QA datasets are the implied evaluation ground (e.g., the question-answering datasets used by Search-R1, R1-Searcher, DeepResearcher). DeepRetrieval is noted to use a restricted real search engine such as PubMed; DeepResearcher trains/evaluates with live web search APIs on open-domain research tasks. Specific dataset names (e.g., HotpotQA-style multi-hop sets) are not enumerated in the survey body. [uncertain on the exact benchmark list, since the survey defers to cited papers.]
benchmark_family: Primarily QA and multi-hop QA (open-domain, knowledge-intensive, deep-research). Tool/search-engine interaction is evaluated via retrieval metrics on a restricted real search engine (PubMed-style) for query-rewriting (DeepRetrieval) and via live web search for open-web research (DeepResearcher). Families touched: QA / multi-hop QA / web-search / deep-research; not embodied (ALFWorld) or code (SWE-bench) families.
baselines: N/A as a survey (no head-to-head experiments of its own). Conceptually it contrasts paradigms: basic/Naive RAG and Advanced/Modular RAG vs Reasoning Agentic RAG; predefined reasoning vs agentic reasoning; prompt-based vs training-based agentic; RAG vs Long-Context LLMs (Self-Route); and Chain-of-Thought vs ReAct (grounded vs purely internal reasoning). It cites that training-based agents (Search-R1, DeepResearcher) outperform RAG baselines and prompt-engineering / static-corpus RL baselines per their source papers.
key_metrics: The survey reports the metrics used by surveyed methods rather than its own. Mentioned: final-answer correctness / exact match and F1 (Search-R1 outcome reward; DeepResearcher F1-based reward); retrieval-quality metrics recall@k, NDCG, and evidence-seeking accuracy Hits@N (DeepRetrieval reward). Reasoning Complexity (Low/Medium/High) and Control Type (Fixed/Adaptive/Agentic) are the survey's own comparison descriptors in Table 2 rather than quantitative metrics.
headline_result: N/A (no single experimental headline number - it is a review). The headline contribution is the two-paradigm taxonomy of Reasoning Agentic RAG: Predefined Reasoning (= cognitive System 1: route-based, loop-based, tree-based, hybrid-modular) vs Agentic Reasoning (= System 2: prompt-based and training-based/RL), summarized in Figure 3 and Table 2, with a cognitive-science dual-process (System 1 / System 2) alignment and an industry-challenge framing.
ablations: N/A (no experiments, hence no ablations). The analytical equivalents are: (1) the predefined-vs-agentic and System-1-vs-System-2 contrast (Table 1); (2) the Control-Type x Reasoning-Complexity comparison across predefined methods (Table 2: Fixed/Adaptive/Agentic; Low/Medium/High); (3) the reward-design comparison across training-based agents (answer reward only for Search-R1; +retrieval/+format/+retry for R1-Searcher/ReZero; retrieval+format for DeepRetrieval; format+answer for DeepResearcher); and (4) training-environment comparison (local retrieval vs restricted vs real-world search engine).
evaluation_decoupling: Partially / surveyed. The survey notes that some methods optimize/report intrinsic retrieval-quality metrics separately (DeepRetrieval rewards recall@k / NDCG / Hits@N) while others use end-to-end outcome metrics only (Search-R1 answer reward; DeepResearcher F1). It does not impose its own decoupled evaluation protocol but documents both intrinsic-retrieval and end-to-end task evaluation across the cited works; it advocates finer-grained process-oriented metrics as future work.
process_vs_outcome_metrics: Surveyed as a tension and an explicit future direction. Most training-based agents use outcome-only rewards (final-answer correctness / EM / F1). The survey argues for finer-grained, PROCESS-oriented reward/evaluation that assesses intermediate steps - document relevance, reasoning coherence, information cross-validation, and effective problem decomposition - because simple outcome rewards under-guide complex multi-step RAG. So it covers both but flags outcome-only as a limitation.
cost_efficiency_tradeoff: Discussed qualitatively and flagged as a key future direction. Self-Route reduces computation cost vs Long-Context models while maintaining performance; RAGate skips unnecessary retrieval for simple turns; route-based/adaptive control avoids redundant operations. The survey calls out 'Improving Efficiency in Retrieval' as a research direction: agents should avoid excessive/unnecessary searches, select promising sources, know when enough has been gathered, and avoid unproductive search loops. No quantitative latency/token/cost numbers are reported by the survey itself.
context_budget_and_selection_count: Surveyed qualitatively. The survey raises the lost-in-the-middle problem for long contexts and the need for adaptive context management; Search-o1's Reason-in-Documents module compresses/distills retrieved content to fit and denoise the reasoning context; fine-grained chunking is noted under Advanced RAG. Selection count k is method-dependent (basic top-k; agentic multi-turn accumulates information across <information> blocks). No single numeric budget or fixed-k policy is prescribed by the survey.
survey_scope_and_axes: Explicit organizing axes: (1) two top-level paradigms - Predefined Reasoning vs Agentic Reasoning (Figure 3 taxonomy); (2) cognitive dual-process alignment System 1 (predefined) vs System 2 (agentic) (Table 1); (3) within Predefined Reasoning, four sub-types: Route-based, Loop-based, Tree-based, Hybrid-modular; (4) within Agentic Reasoning, Prompt-based (function-calling/ReAct, Self-Ask, LRM-based/Search-o1) vs Training-based (RL: local-retrieval, restricted, real-world search engines); (5) comparison descriptors: Control Type (Fixed/Adaptive/Agentic), Reasoning Complexity (Low/Medium/High), Training Environment, Reward Design (Table 2). Coverage: 50 references; time window roughly 2020-2025 (heavy 2024-2025 emphasis), with an explicit industry / enterprise open-source-project lens (DeepSearcher, RAGFlow, Haystack, LightRAG, R2R, FlashRAG, Langchain-Chatchat).
benchmark_construction_and_size: N/A (a survey, not a benchmark paper; it constructs no dataset). It instead curates a paper list and a comparison of ~18 representative methods/projects (Table 2) split across predefined and agentic reasoning.
builds_on: Builds on the foundational RAG line (Lewis et al. 2020) and the Naive->Advanced->Modular RAG framing of Gao et al. (2023, 2024). Predefined-reasoning lineage: RAGate, Self-Route (route-based), Self-RAG, CRAG (loop-based), RAPTOR, MCTS-RAG (tree-based), Adaptive-RAG, Modular-RAG (hybrid-modular). Agentic-reasoning lineage: ReAct, Self-Ask, OpenAI function calling, Search-o1 (prompt-based); Search-R1, R1-Searcher, ReZero, DeepRetrieval, DeepResearcher (RL training-based), themselves built on DeepSeek-R1 / o1-style RL reasoning and PPO/GRPO. Cognitive framing builds on dual-process System 1 / System 2 theory.
contrasts_with: Positions Reasoning Agentic RAG against static/basic RAG pipelines (limited by fixed control logic, no reflection/adaptation). Internally contrasts Predefined Reasoning (System 1, fixed orchestration) vs Agentic Reasoning (System 2, autonomous decision-making); prompt-based vs training-based agentic methods; ReAct's thought-action-observation cycle vs the more direct function-calling style; RAG vs Long-Context LLMs (Self-Route); grounded ReAct vs purely-internal Chain-of-Thought; and DeepRetrieval (optimize a single refined query) vs ReZero (value of multiple retrieval attempts). Distinct from broader RAG surveys (Gao et al.) by focusing specifically on reasoning + agentic tool-use and an industry-challenge lens.
lineage: Surveys group. A focused 2025 survey of Reasoning Agentic RAG, sitting downstream of the foundational RAG survey (Gao et al. 2023) and adjacent to agentic-RAG and reasoning-LLM surveys. It is the canonical reference for the Predefined-Reasoning (System 1) vs Agentic-Reasoning (System 2) dichotomy and for organizing RL-trained search agents (Search-R1/DeepResearcher) alongside prompt-based agentic methods (ReAct/Search-o1); it anchors the reasoning-and-tool-use sub-topic within the broader agentic-RAG / experience-retrieval literature.
cbr_cycle_coverage: N/A (not a case-based-reasoning work; no Retrieve/Reuse/Revise/Retain case cycle. It surveys document/tool retrieval with reasoning, not CBR).
explicit_cbr_grounding: false. The survey does not frame Reasoning Agentic RAG as case-based reasoning and does not cite Aamodt & Plaza / Kolodner; its cognitive grounding is dual-process System 1 / System 2 theory, not CBR.
tool_document_engineering: N/A / lightly touched. The survey is about reasoning over retrieved documents and search tools, not tool-description indexing. Function calling exposes predefined tool/API interfaces integrated into model training/prompt design, and a future direction calls for richer tool configurations (result filtering, sorting, domain specification, structured DB queries), but tool-description embedding/engineering for retrieval is not analyzed.
index_content_separation: N/A as a method, but the related pattern appears via RAPTOR's hierarchical summary tree (search lightweight summaries first, descend to heavier content) and via distillation of retrieved content (Search-o1 Reason-in-Documents). Not framed as a progressive-disclosure / index-then-content efficiency mechanism.
dynamic_index_and_protocol: Partially relevant. Agentic reasoning surveys live tool/search-engine interaction via function calling / built-in tool interfaces (GPT/Gemini) and live web search APIs (DeepResearcher), as opposed to a static document index. However, the survey does not discuss MCP, RapidAPI registries, or CRUD auto-sync of a tool index; the integration protocol is function-calling / search-API invocation. So: live search-engine/API tool use is covered, but not a synchronized tool-registry protocol like MCP.
tool_dependency_awareness: N/A. The survey does not model inter-tool dependencies (output-of-A feeds B, shared auth, prerequisites) or dependency-aware tool retrieval; tool use is primarily single search-engine/API invocation interleaved with reasoning.
adaptation_mechanism: N/A (no CBR case adaptation/revision cycle). The closest analogs are corrective/iterative refinement of retrieval+generation (CRAG query rewriting / web-search fallback, Self-RAG self-critique) and RL fine-tuning of the search policy (Search-R1/ReZero/DeepRetrieval/DeepResearcher), but these refine behavior/context rather than adapt a retrieved case.
